objective.name: length of a string containing every permutation as a contiguous substring
constraints: the string uses exactly the symbols 1 through 7
each of the 5040 permutations of 1 through 7 occurs as a contiguous length-7 substring

best_public.source: Andrei Teodorescu, Superpermutators Google Group post and attachment 5905_7_sol1.txt
best_public.evidence_state: downloaded from the source attachment; all 5040 contiguous permutations independently replayed and length recomputed as 5905
best_public.origin_type: public search result; human/AI contribution not disclosed in the source checked

best_reproduced_human.evidence_state: the recursive construction described by Ashlock and Tillotson was independently implemented, saved, and exactly checked

optimality.status: not established; best construction found in the reviewed sources has length 5905

references.citation: Andrei Teodorescu, n=7 superpermutation of length 5905, Superpermutators Google Group, 2026-08-17
references.finding: The post attaches four words of length 5905. Andrew Balint reported independently checking all 5040 permutations. The source does not disclose AI involvement.

A computer-assisted lower-bound package claims 5901, with a Lean-checked reduction conditional on thirty search equations. Twenty-three of the thirty rely on searches where most are by one program; the README says twenty-three Lean equations are not evaluated. This is not treated here as a fully replayed certificate.

A distinct Lean development states 5898 <= s(7) <= 5906 and has explicit AI-generated authorship disclosure. It independently supports that the exact minimum is unresolved in that artifact, but its upper bound is older than the 5905 construction.

optimality.bound_note: The 5898 lower bound is a formalized computer-assisted result with a native evaluator/compiler trust base. The stronger 5901 result is recorded as conditional computer-assisted evidence and was not independently replayed for this task. No optimality proof is claimed.

source.title: Andrei Teodorescu, n=7 superpermutation of length 5905
source.claim: Four length-5905 strings were posted; Andrew Balint reports verifying each as a complete superpermutation.

best_reproduced.verification_method: strip source attachment whitespace; enumerate all length-7 windows; compare the valid-window set with all 5040 permutations; recompute string length

human_method_baseline.source: Ashlock and Tillotson (1993), Construction of small superpermutations and minimal injective superstrings, Congressus Numerantium 93, 91-98; recursive rule restated in Houston (2014), Section 1, arXiv:1408.5108
